issue: Does a released prisoner's 28 U.S.C. § 2241 challenge to an allegedly excessive prison term remain live (not moot) when the only relief is a speculative possible modification of supervised release under 18 U.S.C. § 3583(e)?

sides.position: A released prisoner's over-incarceration claim is not moot because the sentencing court could modify the supervised-release term under § 3583(e) to provide relief.

A released prisoner's over-incarceration claim is moot or too speculative to decide, because a possible future modification of supervised release under § 3583(e) does not provide a live case or controversy.
cases: United States v. Bundy, 391 F. App'x 886 (D.C. Cir. 2010)

this_court: Side 2: this court expressly departs from its own prior decision in Johnson v. Pettiford and holds the speculative possibility of a § 3583(e) modification does not keep the claim alive.
quote: Moreover, Johnson v. Pettiford sits at the center of a circuit split.
